findings.reason: the node's goal is preventing destruction, which writes and deletes cover and the done-when tests directly; the read clause is wording, and correcting the sentence would not alter the deliverable, the done-when or any dispatched work.
findings.text: the Deliverable says a worker "can then read, write and delete only inside its own scratch directory", but the mechanism named in the same sentence is a read-only bind, which withholds writes and deletions only: a `--ro-bind` of the scratch root leaves every sibling run's scratch directory (and the rest of the filesystem the `--dev-bind / /` opens) readable, so the stated read-restriction is broader than what the fence produces

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `fence_argv`, `_fence_write_roots`, `delivery_write_roots`, `worker_scratch_root()`/`worker_scratch_dir(run_id)`, the three fenced call sites and the three cited run ids all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §9 declares a negative control (un-sealing the scratch root makes the sibling `rm -rf` succeed and the test fail) and each arm is falsifiable at base.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate log and the declared negative-control log are written under the run directory, and the incident evidence sits on the durable reports tree, not a node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test path and the touched modules carry no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the §9 deliverable states a property (reads restricted to the run's own scratch) that the mechanism it names does not produce.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §9 carries one deliverable: seal the worker scratch root and hand the run its own scratch directory as a write root.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §9 needs only shipped machinery (the §3 protected set, `_fence_write_roots`, and the `TMPDIR`-to-run-scratch wiring at `dispatch_launch.py:897`), all present; it declares no per-node edge that points at the wrong node.
